title: Proper locally acyclic morphisms have invertible higher-image specialization
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $G$ a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; torsion means every local section is locally killed by a positive integer. Suppose $f$ is locally acyclic relative to $G$ [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]. Then for every integer $q\ge0$, every geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$, and every geometric point $\bar t$ of $S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the canonical specialization homomorphism
$$\operatorname{sp}:(R^qf_*G)_{\bar s}\longrightarrow(R^qf_*G)_{\bar t}$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Here the target stalk is at the composite geometric point of $S$, higher direct images are computed in abelian sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], stalks are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and specialization is the homomorphism obtained by restricting pointed etale neighbourhood germs through $S_{(\bar s)}\to S$. No smoothness or local constancy of $G$ is assumed, nor any finiteness of its stalks.

source.place: Tag 0GJW, lemma-sp-isom-proper-torsion-loc-ac, specialization for K=G[0] and degree-q cohomology

proof.text: Fix $\bar s,\bar t$ and use the schemes and maps $S',X',p,i,h$ of [lem-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-closed-fibre-unit], with $G'=p^{-1}G$ and $K=G[0]$. The ring defining $S'$ is strictly henselian and the lift of $\bar s$ lies over its closed point by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1). The base change $f':X'\to S'$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Both $f$ and $f'$ are qcqs: their finite-type condition gives quasi-compactness; their diagonal is a closed immersion, whose inverse image of an affine open is affine and hence quasi-compact, giving quasi-separatedness. These are exactly the definitions in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The morphism $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to S'$ is between affine schemes, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]; its base change $h$ is affine and therefore qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1),(3).

source.place: Tag 0GJW, lemma-sp-isom-proper-torsion-loc-ac, setup of f prime and h; affine qcqs verification

proof.text: For any proper $v:Z\to T$ and any bounded below abelian etale complex $E$ with torsion cohomology, apply [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] to the cartesian square over a geometric point $u:P\to T$. It gives $u^{-1}Rv_*E\cong Ra_{u,*}(E|_{Z_u})$. Apply $R\Gamma(P,-)$ and [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit](1) to $a_u:Z_u\to P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], global sections on $P$ are exact and naturally identify $\Gamma(P,u^{-1}F)$ with $F_u$. Exact inverse image is computed termwise by [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]; thus applying these exact functors termwise gives the derived stalk on the left. We obtain the canonical fibre isomorphism $\rho_u:(Rv_*E)_u\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Z_u,E|_{Z_u})$, and it is the exchange fibre map by construction. Apply this to $v=f$, $E=K$, at both $u=\bar s$ and the composite point $u=\bar t$ of $S$. The hypothesis holds because $K$ has only $G$ as its cohomology sheaf. Hence both $\rho_{\bar s}$ and $\rho_{\bar t}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-specialization-cospecialization-compatibility] are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0GJW proof, first sentence; Tag 0DDF, lemma-proper-base-change-stalk (2)

proof.text: The hypothesis of local acyclicity applies directly to [lem-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-closed-fibre-unit]: $i^{-1}\beta:i^{-1}G'[0]\to i^{-1}Rh_*(G_{\bar t}[0])$ is invertible. Put $K'=Rh_*(G_{\bar t}[0])$. It is bounded below because the derived direct image in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] maps $D^+$ to $D^+$. The pullback $G_{\bar t}$ is torsion: [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies each stalk with a stalk of $G$, so each element has a positive annihilator. Apply [lem-sbc-qcqs-higher-images-prime-torsion] to $h$ (qcqs by step 1) and $G_{\bar t}$, with $\mathcal P$ the set of all primes. It says every stalk element of every $R^nh_*G_{\bar t}$ has a positive annihilator, which is the torsion sheaf condition. Explicitly, a stalk germ killed by $m$ has a representative killed by $m$ on some pointed etale neighbourhood, by the filtered-colimit definition of a stalk; these neighbourhoods, for all geometric points of a given section, supply the required local annihilators. The cohomology sheaves of $K'$ are these higher images, so all are torsion. No finite stalks or common annihilator have been used.

source.place: Tag 0GJW proof, K prime; Tag 0DDD, lemma-torsion-direct-image (1), using the existing fixed-prime version

proof.text: Apply the fibre comparison of step 2 to $f'$ and $K'$ at the closed geometric point $\bar s$ of $S'$. Properness is supplied by step 1, and boundedness below and torsion by step 3. Its source $(Rf'_*K')_{\bar s}$ identifies canonically with $R\Gamma(X',K')$: by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-etale-acyclic], $\Gamma(S',-)$ is exact, and by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] it is naturally the closed stalk functor; apply this natural isomorphism termwise to a representative of $Rf'_*K'$, then use the Leray identification [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit](1). Under this identification the fibre map is restriction along $i$. To check this on the actual morphism, choose a bounded below K-injective representative $I$ of $K'$ and a K-injective resolution $j:i^{-1}I\to J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise], the fibre exchange is represented by the termwise underived exchange followed by the direct image of $j$. For each degree $r$, the closed stalk of $f'_*I^r$ is identified with $(f'_*I^r)(S')=I^r(X')$ by the germ map of [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk]. A global section $a\in I^r(X')$ represents this germ at the pointed neighbourhood $S'$. The representative formula in [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], with this neighbourhood and $V=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, sends it to its restriction in $(i^{-1}I^r)(X_{\bar s})$. Following by $j$ therefore gives the complex map $\Gamma(X',I)\to\Gamma(X_{\bar s},i^{-1}I)\to\Gamma(X_{\bar s},J)$, which is the derived pullback along $i$ by [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] (equivalently the derived-unit formula of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit](2)). Thus the exchange fibre map agrees with restriction, including the resolution comparison maps. Therefore the actual restriction morphism $R\Gamma(X',K')\to R\Gamma(X_{\bar s},i^{-1}K')$ is invertible. Following it by $R\Gamma(X_{\bar s},(i^{-1}\beta)^{-1})$, and preceding it by the inverse Leray identification $R\Gamma(X_{\bar t},G_{\bar t}[0])\cong R\Gamma(X',K')$, gives the specified $cosp$. All three factors are isomorphisms, so $cosp$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0GJW proof, displayed restriction map and strict henselian source identification

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-specialization-cospecialization-compatibility], $cosp\,\rho_{\bar t}\,sp=\rho_{\bar s}$ for the pointed-neighbourhood specialization map. Steps 2 and 4 make the three other arrows invertible. Thus $sp=\rho_{\bar t}^{-1}cosp^{-1}\rho_{\bar s}$ is an isomorphism. Apply degree-$q$ cohomology. The exact geometric inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], followed by exact global sections over the geometric point from [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], preserves kernels, images and their quotient, so $H^q((Rf_*G[0])_u)=(R^qf_*G)_u$. Termwise pointed-neighbourhood restriction induces exactly the homomorphism in the item, because specialization there is defined by those same germ restrictions. Hence the claimed homomorphism is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$.
